clusters.name: Targeted sensing and localized actuation
clusters.description: Detect stain location or soil concentration and apply localized interventions (micro-sprays, heated spots, electrowetting, local mechanical actuators) to treat only contaminated areas and minimize overall water use.

clusters.name: Localized controlled dosing and triggered release
clusters.description: Deliver concentrated actives or cleaning payloads on demand at specific sites via micro-dosing, microcapsules, thin films, or triggered carriers that release chemistry only where needed.

clusters.name: Phase-change and advanced solvent extraction
clusters.description: Use vapor/condensation cycles, pressurization swings, or non-traditional solvent states (near-/supercritical, vapor-phase cleaning) to dissolve and transport contaminants without saturating textiles with bulk water.

clusters.name: Flow- and suction-driven extraction
clusters.description: Remove loosened soils by moving fluids or gases through or away from textiles (pressure flushing, gentle continuous extraction flows, vacuum/pneumatic suction) to carry contaminants out with minimal liquid volume.

clusters.name: Acoustic and impulse detachment
clusters.description: Use high-frequency vibrations, ultrasound, surface acoustic waves, shockwaves, or pulsed-air impulses to fracture soil–fiber bonds and eject or loosen contaminants for collection without large water volumes.

clusters.name: Mechanical agitation and solid-contact abrasion
clusters.description: Apply relative motion, tumbling, collisions, textured pads or solid abrasives to mechanically dislodge or transfer soils from fabric surfaces for subsequent low-water removal.

clusters.name: Foam- and bubble-mediated flotation and lift
clusters.description: Use foamed media or bubbles that attach to hydrophobic particles and lift or float soils away from fibers for collection, minimizing wetting of the bulk textile.

clusters.name: Field-driven particle transport and capture
clusters.description: Use electric, ionic, electrophoretic, dielectrophoretic or magnetic fields to move, concentrate, or capture charged/magnetic particles for later removal without relying on bulk solvent transport.

clusters.name: Field-modulated fluid rheology
clusters.description: Change transport fluid properties (viscosity, viscoelasticity) via additives or applied fields so fluid stresses preferentially release adhered particles while minimizing required water volume.

clusters.name: Chemical solubilization, adsorption and sequestration
clusters.description: Apply surfactants, enzymes, chelators, adsorbents or engineered sorbents that solubilize, digest, bind or sequester soils into removable phases that reduce rinse volume; includes sorbent regeneration.

clusters.name: Electrochemical and plasma-driven transformations
clusters.description: Use electrical or plasma processes (electrocoagulation, in-situ oxidant or plasma generation) to chemically alter, aggregate, or decompose contaminants to aid low-water removal.

clusters.name: Stimulus-responsive surface release and removable coatings
clusters.description: Temporarily change fabric/fiber surface adhesion via smart coatings or apply sacrificial peelable films that bind soils and are removed, enabling capture or low-water extraction of contaminants.

clusters.name: Continuous purification and recirculation
clusters.description: Separate contaminants from the transport fluid in real time (filtration, trapping, recovery) and return cleaned solvent/water for immediate reuse to reduce net water consumption.
